Key work

Development and clinical validation of cerebrospinal fluid and blood biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease and neuronal injury.

  • CSF tau and amyloid-β. Early studies showed elevated tau in Alzheimer's disease CSF, and a community-based study established the diagnostic value of CSF tau and Aβ42 in clinical practice.
  • Clinical implementation. Established age-specific reference values for CSF tau and Aβ42 and assessed the performance and complications of lumbar puncture in memory clinics, where few patients required medical intervention for complications.
  • Blood phosphorylated tau. Developed plasma p-tau181 and p-tau231 assays that identify Alzheimer's disease pathology, with p-tau231 rising at the earliest stages of amyloid-β accumulation.
  • Synaptic and injury markers. CSF neurogranin correlated with cognitive decline in prodromal Alzheimer's disease, and blood biomarkers of brain injury were elevated in concussed professional ice hockey players.

Key findings

Tags
Sort
  1. 1
    AUC 0.90–0.98for a blood p-tau181 test separating Alzheimer's from healthy older adults

    A new blood test for tau phosphorylated at position 181 (p-tau181), tested in 1,131 people from four cohorts, rose step by step along the course of Alzheimer's disease. It separated Alzheimer's dementia from cognitively healthy older adults with an AUC of 0.90 to 0.98, told it apart from other brain diseases such as frontotemporal and vascular dementia, and predicted memory decline and shrinkage of the hippocampus over 1 year.

    Karikari et al. 2020 · Lancet NeurolAssay development and validation in 4 prospective cohorts, 1,131 participants
  2. 2
    83%of people with mild memory problems who later got Alzheimer's were flagged by spinal fluid tests

    In 750 people with mild cognitive impairment from 12 centres in Europe and the US, spinal fluid amyloid-β42, total tau and p-tau together identified those who went on to develop Alzheimer's dementia with 83% sensitivity and 72% specificity. Accuracy was lower than in single-centre studies because results varied between labs, showing a need for standardized testing.

    Mattsson et al. 2009 · JAMAMulticentre prospective cohort, 750 people with MCI, 529 with Alzheimer's, 304 controls
  3. 3
    Before PETblood p-tau231 rises before an amyloid scan turns positive

    A blood test for p-tau231 identified Alzheimer's with an AUC of 0.92 to 0.94 against healthy amyloid-negative adults and, in samples taken about 4 years before death, matched the brain autopsy diagnosis with an AUC of 0.99. Its levels started to rise with only slight amyloid build-up, earlier than the usual amyloid PET threshold and earlier than blood p-tau181.

    Ashton et al. 2021 · Acta NeuropatholAssay development and validation in 4 cohorts, 588 participants, including an autopsy cohort
  4. 4
    Earliestblood markers of amyloid build-up in people without symptoms

    In cognitively healthy adults of the ALFA+ cohort, all six blood markers tested changed in preclinical Alzheimer's, but p-tau231 became abnormal at the lowest amyloid level. p-tau231 and p-tau217 tracked amyloid in the brain regions affected first and predicted later amyloid increases, making them candidates to screen people for prevention trials.

    Milà-Alomà et al. 2022 · Nat MedCohort study of cognitively unimpaired adults with amyloid PET, ALFA+ (Barcelona)
  5. 5
    88%of Alzheimer's patients had high phosphorylated tau in spinal fluid

    An early study of tau in spinal fluid found phosphorylated tau about 3.5 times higher in Alzheimer's than in healthy controls, and above the control cut-off in 35 of 40 patients. Levels were normal in Parkinson's disease and depression, but overlapped with vascular and frontal lobe dementia.

    Blennow et al. 1995 · Mol Chem NeuropatholCase-control study of spinal fluid tau across dementia types, 40 Alzheimer's patients
  6. 6
    94%of probable Alzheimer's found by spinal fluid tau and amyloid-β42 in everyday practice

    When spinal fluid tau and amyloid-β42 were run weekly as routine tests for all 241 patients seen for memory problems at a Swedish community hospital, they detected 94% of probable Alzheimer's and 75% of mild cognitive impairment. With Alzheimer's present in about 45% of patients, a positive result was right 90% of the time and a negative result 95%. Specificity was lower in Lewy body (67%) and vascular dementia (48%).

    Andreasen et al. 2001 · Arch NeurolProspective 1-year study of consecutive patients, 241 people, Piteå, Sweden
  7. 7
    Stableamyloid-β42 in spinal fluid stays low through the course of Alzheimer's

    Spinal fluid amyloid-β42 was less than half the control level in Alzheimer's, and 92% of patients had low values. Levels a year apart in the same person correlated at r = 0.90 and did not depend on how long or how severe the dementia was, so the test is also low in mild, early disease.

    Andreasen et al. 1999 · Arch Neurol20-month prospective study, 53 Alzheimer's patients and 21 controls
  8. 8
    Aβ42/40 ratiopredicts Alzheimer's better than amyloid-β42 alone

    Following 137 people with mild cognitive impairment for 4 to 6 years, those who developed Alzheimer's had lower spinal fluid amyloid-β42 and a lower amyloid-β42/40 ratio at the start. The ratio identified future Alzheimer's better than amyloid-β42 alone.

    Hansson et al. 2007 · Dement Geriatr Cogn DisordProspective cohort, 137 people with MCI followed 4-6 years
  9. 9
    Up to 11.5×higher risk of dementia with abnormal automated spinal fluid tests

    Using automated Elecsys tests in 1,050 people with memory symptoms but no dementia (ADNI and BioFINDER), those with abnormal results declined faster and had a 1.7 to 11.5 times higher risk of progressing to Alzheimer's or dementia. The tau to amyloid-β42 ratios worked best and gave the same cut-offs in both cohorts.

    Blennow et al. 2019 · Sci RepAnalysis of 2 multicentre longitudinal cohorts, 1,050 patients
  10. 10
    Tracks declineblood neurofilament light rises with nerve cell loss in Alzheimer's

    In 1,583 ADNI participants with yearly blood samples for up to 11 years, neurofilament light was higher in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's dementia and rose fastest in dementia. Faster increases went with faster brain shrinkage, lower brain energy use and faster cognitive decline, so the blood test could monitor nerve damage in drug trials.

    Mattsson et al. 2019 · JAMA NeurolLongitudinal multicentre cohort, 1,583 participants, ADNI
  11. 11
    12.8×higher risk of Alzheimer's dementia with high spinal fluid neurogranin

    Neurogranin, a protein from the receiving side of synapses, was markedly raised in spinal fluid in Alzheimer's dementia in three independent cohorts. In mild cognitive impairment, high neurogranin predicted progression to Alzheimer's dementia (hazard ratio 12.8) and faster cognitive decline in amyloid-positive patients.

    Kvartsberg et al. 2015 · Alzheimers DementNew assay tested in 3 clinical cohorts, 100 Alzheimer's, 40 MCI, 80 controls
  12. 12
    Low riskof complications from lumbar puncture in memory clinics

    Among 3,868 patients having a lumbar puncture at 23 memory clinics, 9% had a typical post-puncture headache, but only 0.3% needed a blood patch and 0.7% were hospitalized. A history of headache raised the risk, while an atraumatic needle and age over 65 lowered it.

    Duits et al. 2016 · Alzheimers DementProspective multicentre study, 3,868 patients, 23 memory clinics
  13. 13
    Age-specificnormal values for spinal fluid tau

    In 231 healthy adults aged 21 to 93, spinal fluid tau rose with age, so normal limits were set by age group (below 300 ng/L at 21-50, 450 at 51-70 and 500 at 71-93). Amyloid-β42 did not change with age, with a normal value above 500 ng/L.

    Sjögren et al. 2001 · Clin ChemReference-value study, 231 healthy adults aged 21-93
  14. 14
    7 to 35 pg/mLupper normal blood neurofilament light from childhood to old age

    Pooling healthy people aged 5 to 90 from eight cohorts, blood neurofilament light rose strongly with age, so upper normal limits were set by age, from 7 pg/mL in children to 35 pg/mL after age 70, to help doctors read the test.

    Simrén et al. 2022 · Brain CommunPooled reference-value study, 8 cohorts of neurologically healthy people aged 5-90
  15. 15
    Concussiondetected by blood neurofilament light in boxers and hockey players

    Blood neurofilament light was higher in amateur boxers 7 to 10 days after a bout than after 3 months of rest, and highest in those who took more than 15 head hits or were groggy. In professional ice hockey players it rose after concussion, returned to normal at return to play, and separated players whose symptoms cleared quickly from those with prolonged symptoms.

    Shahim et al. 2017 · Neurology2 prospective cohorts, 14 boxers and 35 hockey players, plus 26 controls
  16. 16
    AUC 0.99blood neurofilament light detecting severe head injury

    In 72 patients with severe traumatic brain injury, blood neurofilament light on admission separated patients from controls with an AUC of 0.99, and the initial level predicted poor outcome 12 months later. The older marker S100B did not predict outcome.

    Shahim et al. 2016 · Sci RepAssay development and prospective study, 72 patients with severe TBI and 35 controls
  17. 17
    Lower tauin spinal fluid after anti-amyloid antibody treatment

    In two 12-month placebo-controlled trials in mild to moderate Alzheimer's, patients given the anti-amyloid antibody bapineuzumab had lower spinal fluid p-tau than those on placebo, with a similar trend for total tau. It was the first evidence that removing amyloid with an antibody may affect downstream nerve damage.

    Blennow et al. 2012 · Arch NeurolBiomarker analysis of 2 phase 2 randomized placebo-controlled trials, 46 patients
  18. 18
    Tangle markera tau fragment in spinal fluid tracks tau PET

    A tau fragment cut at amino acid 368 was found inside tangles, and its share of total tau in spinal fluid was lower in Alzheimer's in three cohorts. The lower the ratio, the more tau showed on tau PET, making it a candidate fluid marker of tangle pathology.

    Blennow et al. 2020 · BrainMass spectrometry, new assay and tau PET in 3 cohorts, 95 Alzheimer's and 76 controls
  19. 19
    Alzheimer's-specificrise of the synapse protein GAP-43 in spinal fluid

    Spinal fluid GAP-43, a protein from the sending side of synapses, was higher in 275 Alzheimer's patients than in controls and in most other brain diseases. In autopsy-confirmed cases it rose with the amount of plaques and tangles, but not with α-synuclein or TDP-43 pathology.

    Sandelius et al. 2019 · Alzheimers DementNew assay in 662 people, with neuropathology in 93
  20. 20
    AD profile in 52%of people with only subjective memory complaints

    In 20 European memory clinics, an Alzheimer's pattern in spinal fluid was found in 52% of people with subjective memory complaints, 68% with non-amnestic and 79% with amnestic mild cognitive impairment, compared with 31% of healthy controls. In amnestic MCI the pattern strongly predicted Alzheimer's dementia (odds ratio 26.8).

    Visser et al. 2009 · Lancet NeurolProspective multicentre cohort (DESCRIPA), 168 patients and 89 controls, up to 3 years
  21. 21
    Inflammation firstraised TNF-α in spinal fluid before Alzheimer's dementia

    Among 56 people with mild cognitive impairment, only those who progressed to Alzheimer's within 9 months had higher spinal fluid levels of the inflammatory signal TNF-α than controls, along with lower anti-inflammatory TGF-β and lower amyloid-β42, pointing to brain inflammation as an early event.

    Tarkowski et al. 2003 · J Neurol Neurosurg PsychiatryProspective study, 56 people with MCI and 25 controls
  22. 22
    Total tau ≠ p-tauafter a stroke, total tau rises but p-tau does not

    After acute stroke, spinal fluid total tau rose to more than 4 times baseline at 3 weeks and returned to normal by 3 to 5 months, while p-tau did not change. This suggests total tau reflects how much nerve cells are damaged, and p-tau reflects tangle-related tau changes.

    Hesse et al. 2001 · Neurosci LettLongitudinal spinal fluid sampling in 9 stroke patients
  23. 23
    OR 2.24per 100 pg/mL lower amyloid-β42, for decline in healthy older women

    In 55 women aged 70 to 84 without dementia in the Gothenburg women's study, lower spinal fluid amyloid-β42 measured in 1992 predicted a larger drop in memory scores over 8 years and was the only predictor of marked decline or dementia.

    Gustafson et al. 2007 · J Neurol Neurosurg PsychiatryPopulation-based prospective cohort, 55 women followed 8 years
  24. 24
    Synapse losstracks dementia severity, plaques do not

    In brain tissue, the synapse protein rab3a was reduced to 60% of control levels in the hippocampus in Alzheimer's, and lower levels went with longer and more severe dementia. Plaque counts were not related to dementia severity, and synapse loss did not differ by APOE4 status.

    Blennow et al. 1996 · J Neural Transm (Vienna)Post-mortem brain study, 19 Alzheimer's patients and 9 controls
  25. 25
    No damagefound after repeated exposure to blasts from heavy weapons

    Army officers exposed to up to 150 blasts from firing heavy weapons or detonating explosives showed normal spinal fluid and blood markers of nerve, glial and blood-brain barrier damage, compared with unexposed controls.

    Blennow et al. 2011 · Acta Neurol Scand3 controlled exposure studies in army officers, 19 unexposed controls

About this page

This page gathers Kaj Blennow's published papers and preprints from PubMed and Europe PMC. The summary and key findings are written from those papers, and every finding cites exactly one of them.

"Most important" puts the findings with the widest relevance first. "Newest" sorts by the year of each finding's paper.

This site is for education and is not medical advice.
